model.name: Credit risk scorer
model.description: Reference consumer-credit decline model. Non-linear with a utilization × debt-to-income leverage interaction and an accelerating sub-prime penalty.

runs.sentence: It is one of Kaimei's built-in reference models, which Kaimei runs itself.

output.name: decision
output.sentence: It answers approve or decline: decline when its chance of decline is at or above 50%, and approve otherwise.

holdings.label: Reference data
holdings.detail: 600 rows uploaded: the population explanations and drift compare against.

holdings.label: Logged predictions
holdings.detail: 196 predictions logged with time, input and output, the first 14 days ago and the latest today.

holdings.label: Realised outcomes
holdings.detail: 173 logged predictions have the real outcome attached.

holdings.label: Decision records
holdings.detail: 17 decisions of 196 logged have a record that says how the model reached it, with a fingerprint.

holdings.label: Stored analyses
holdings.detail: 1 analysis stored with options, seed and model version, the latest today.

holdings.label: Model structure
holdings.detail: No structure is uploaded, so the model's layers and weights are not held and cannot be exported.

findings.name: Global importance
findings.title: Global feature importance
findings.summary: `credit_score` is the most influential input, followed by `utilization` and `debt_to_income`. Together they carry 58% of the measured importance (permutation importance over 400 rows).

findings.name: Learned rules
findings.title: What the model has learned
findings.summary: Higher `credit_score` decreases the probability of decline, most sharply between 563 and 612 (range 11% → 86%).

findings.name: Behaviour curves
findings.title: Feature behaviour curves
findings.summary: Behaviour curves for the 6 most important features. 6 respond monotonically.

findings.name: Interactions
findings.title: Feature interactions
findings.summary: The strongest interaction is between `income` and `loan_amount` (6% of their joint effect is non-additive).

findings.name: Robustness
findings.title: Robustness to input noise
findings.summary: 2.1% of decisions flip under 5%-σ input noise. Most fragile inputs: `credit_score`, `income`.

findings.name: Drift
findings.title: Input drift
findings.summary: Recent traffic has significant drift (PSI 0.85). Shifted inputs: `debt_to_income`, `utilization`, `employment_years`, `age`.

findings.name: Output behaviour
findings.title: Output behaviour
findings.summary: On 400 reference rows the model predicts `decline` 41% of the time; 18% of cases sit within ±0.10 of the decision threshold.

findings.name: Performance against outcomes
findings.title: Performance against outcomes
findings.summary: AUC on the latest 60 outcomes is 0.609, down from 0.868 on the 113 outcomes before them. That is worse by more than chance explains (z = -3.1).

evidence.name: EU AI Act
evidence.scope: The Act places its heaviest obligations on high-risk AI systems, such as those that evaluate the creditworthiness of people. Whether this model is part of one, and from when the obligations apply, is for you and your counsel.
evidence.sentence: Evidence held toward 6 of 9 requirements, partly held for 3.

evidence.scope: In the United States, a creditor that takes adverse action on a credit application gives the applicant a statement of specific reasons, or tells them they can ask for one. Whether a decision of this model is such an action is for you and your counsel.
